clue.text: 12 — former philosopher and historian

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
David Hume, the Scottish philosopher, also wrote a celebrated History of England

explanation.surface: A puzzle entry described as a long-dead thinker who also chronicled the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 12 across, UNEARTH; EX plus HUME gives EXHUME, which means to dig up.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume a body is to dig it out of the grave, the same act as bringing something up out of the ground.

clue.text: Advocacy of marriage

blocks.note: first meaning: taking up and supporting a cause
second meaning: a wedding or betrothal

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as campaigning for marriage, but the two nouns are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Espousing a cause means supporting it, and to espouse someone is, more traditionally, to wed them.

clue.text: Reap reward initially in own way

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it
in places that letter inside the following words

blocks.note: the opening letter of reward
to own something is to have it
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone collects their prize, first of all, by doing it their own way.
explanation.definitionFit: To harvest is to gather a crop, which is what reaping is.

clue.text: Notes from member, each containing instant cash

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so the following words sit inside the word before

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for member, as in MP
ea is the abbreviation for each
a mo is a moment, an instant
the rand is the South African currency

explanation.surface: A councillor's memos, each one enclosing ready money.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda, the plural of memorandum, are written notes or reminders.

clue.text: A rabble-rouser, but a good mixer, we hope

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who stirs up a crowd
second meaning: the paddle or device in a washing machine or tank that stirs the contents

explanation.surface: A troublemaker who is, one hopes, nonetheless sociable at parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good mixer' suggests a sociable person; read literally, it is a machine part that churns things round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a political stirrer and a stirring paddle in a washing machine or vat carry this name.

clue.text: Have revenge — inflict punishment on a fellow team member

definitions.text: inflict punishment on a fellow team member

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for retaliating

blocks.clueFragment: inflict punishment on a fellow team member
blocks.note: second meaning: read literally, attack one's own back, a defensive player in football or rugby on one's own side

explanation.walkthrough: In rugby and football the backs are players behind the forwards; hitting one of your own side would be getting your own back.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to retaliate against someone who wronged you, taking revenge.

clue.text: Bird's claw found in part of a lock

blocks.note: first meaning: the hooked claw of a bird of prey
second meaning: the shoulder of a lock bolt that the key turns against

explanation.surface: A bird's claw discovered lodged inside a door lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' might suggest hair or a canal, but this is the locksmith's term for the shoulder on the bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the claw of a raptor, and also the name for the projection on a lock bolt.

clue.text: Get thin, possibly, and become more tense

indicators.note: possibly suggests one arrangement among others, so these letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing weight might make a dieter grow more anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or muscle that is drawn taut is strained, a plain synonym for growing tense.

clue.text: Goes over again and removes daughter from military police

indicators.note: removes says a letter is taken away from the following word

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogies
redcaps is the nickname for British military police, from their red caps

explanation.surface: Someone repeats themselves and gets a daughter released from army custody.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcaps is the British slang for the Royal Military Police.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or go over the main points again.

clue.text: After breaking into plants, criminals act with undue haste

indicators.note: breaking into puts this word inside the next

blocks.note: on can mean after, as in 'on reflection'
rushes are marsh plants
fences are criminals who receive and sell stolen goods

explanation.surface: Burglars who smashed into a greenhouse behaved recklessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word; it gives ON. Rushing one's fences is a hunting image of a rider taking jumps too fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushing one's fences means tackling problems too hastily, before one is properly ready.

clue.text: Mistress detailed books of the greatest significance

indicators.note: de-tailed reads as 'with its tail removed', so the last letter of the word goes

blocks.note: a paramour is an illicit lover
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A lover gave a detailed account of the most important books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'thorough', but it means curtailed: PARAMOUR loses its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount describes whatever is supreme or ranks above all else in importance.

clue.text: Retired officer accepts soldier's method of reasoning

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the officer's abbreviation is read backwards
accepting something means taking it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Col is the abbreviation for colonel
a GI is an American soldier; the 's is read as 'is', joining the clue

explanation.surface: A pensioned colonel takes on board a private's way of thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the discipline of sound argument, the systematic way of drawing conclusions.

clue.text: Dig up a hunter that works

indicators.note: works can mean is worked, kneaded into new shape, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go and find a hunting animal that actually does its job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a working terrier or horse; 'that works' instead tells you to rework the seven letters of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to bring out of the ground by digging, or figuratively to discover something hidden.

clue.text: Continuous directions grasped by Bottom only?

indicators.note: something grasped is held inside the hands, so these letters sit within the other piece

blocks.note: N and S are the compass points north and south
if there is only a bottom, there is no top; the question mark flags the playful reading

explanation.surface: Stage instructions endlessly taken in by Bottom, the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom looks like Shakespeare's character, but it describes something with no top.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-stop means going on without a break, which is what continuous describes.

clue.text: It's mostly functioning as a protein

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: acting can mean operating or functioning, as in acting as a brake

explanation.surface: Something said to work, for the most part, as a protein.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTIN is a protein found in muscle fibres, working with myosin to make them contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Actin is a structural muscle protein that forms the thin filaments involved in contraction.

clue.text: It restricts movement at the head of the bay

definitions.text: It restricts movement at the head of the bay

blocks.clueFragment: It restricts movement at the head of the bay
blocks.note: surface reading: a boom or barrier across the mouth of a bay, limiting shipping
setter's reading: a bay is a brown horse, and the strap goes round its head

explanation.surface: A harbour barrier controlling ships entering at the top of the bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay' suggests a stretch of coast; it is a reddish-brown horse, and the strap round its nose keeps its jaw closed.
explanation.definitionFit: A noseband is the part of a horse's bridle encircling the nose, keeping the mouth shut on the bit.

clue.text: Pub ban imposed on Scotsman — he's a lout

indicators.note: in a down clue, being imposed on something means placed above it

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
to bar is to ban
Ian is a typically Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scot barred from his local turns out to be a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbarian is an uncivilised, coarse person, much the same as an oafish lout.

clue.text: Priest always embracing students is a party-goer

indicators.note: an embrace holds something within the arms, so the next word goes inside

blocks.note: Rev is the abbreviation for Reverend
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate, so two Ls are students

explanation.surface: A clergyman who is constantly surrounded by undergraduates likes his parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller is someone enjoying lively festivities, which is what a party-goer does.

clue.text: Game bird, as used to feed animals

indicators.note: food goes into an animal, so this word is put inside the others

blocks.note: two animals: a cur is a mongrel dog, and a sow is a female pig
taken as written

explanation.surface: A game bird being fed to farm animals as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The curassow is a large turkey-like bird of Central and South America, hunted for food.

clue.text: Parvenu requires opening after going to London

indicators.note: after places the first piece behind the second in the answer

blocks.note: in Britain one goes up to London, the capital, from anywhere else
an opening is a start

explanation.surface: A newcomer needs a break once he has moved to the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu and an upstart are both people who have risen suddenly to wealth or status and behave arrogantly.

clue.text: Inspect troops, say, for entertainment

indicators.note: say signals that the word for the inspection is to be spoken, giving a different spelling

blocks.note: to review troops is to inspect them formally on parade

explanation.surface: A parade inspection staged as a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical show of sketches, songs and dances, a form of light stage entertainment.

clue.text: The guts displayed in half a dozen rough races?

indicators.note: rough suggests something crudely handled, so these letters are roughed up into a new order

blocks.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A display of nerve in six bruising contests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The guts' seems to mean courage, as the surface's rough races suggest; it means innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscera are the internal organs of the body, especially those in the abdomen.

clue.text: Rook in tree is in rear of gun

indicators.note: in places the letter for the chess piece inside the word for the tree

blocks.note: R is the chess notation for rook
the beech is a common tree

explanation.surface: A rook perched in a tree sits behind a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' suggests the bird, natural in a tree; it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The breech is the back part of a gun barrel, where the cartridge is loaded.

clue.text: Soldiers do duty as Terriers

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to serve is to do one's duty in the forces

explanation.surface: Troops performing their duty as part of the Territorial Army.
explanation.walkthrough: Terriers is a nickname for members of Britain's Territorial Army, its part-time volunteer force, which is the army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Territorials form Britain's army reserve, part-time soldiers who back up the regular forces.

clue.text: Electronic device requires part for a diode

indicators.note: part says only a section of the following words is needed

blocks.note: the letters run across the words in sequence

explanation.surface: A gadget needs a component for its diode.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio is a receiver of broadcast signals, an electronic device built from components like diodes.

clue.text: Club restaurant used without hesitation

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the hesitation's letters are taken out

blocks.note: a brasserie is an informal French-style restaurant
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A members' club whose dining room was used with no hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society; it is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie is an old name for a wooden golf club, roughly a two-wood, once with a brass sole plate.

clue.text: The creature comes from Louisiana after all!

indicators.note: the state's abbreviation emerges from within the other word, which surrounds it

blocks.note: LA is the postal abbreviation for the US state Louisiana
the end is what comes after everything else

explanation.surface: Astonishment that some animal turns out to be from Louisiana, after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After all' reads as 'nevertheless', but it is the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, so it is a creature in the sense of an animal.

clue.text: Colouring obtained from fowl and fish, it's said

indicators.note: said tells us the bird and fish words are to be spoken aloud

blocks.note: a Cochin is a large breed of domestic chicken; an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A dye apparently extracted from poultry and seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Cochineal is a crimson food colouring made from crushed scale insects.

clue.text: A place for plants and stolen game

blocks.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
house, or housey-housey, is an old name for bingo

explanation.surface: A greenhouse alongside poached game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stolen game' reads as poached animals, but it is two separate pieces; house is the British forces' name for bingo.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothouse is a heated greenhouse where tender plants are grown.

clue.text: Not just an amusement park — not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is absent

blocks.note: a funfair is a travelling fair of rides and stalls

explanation.surface: Something more than merely a theme park, though not at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not just' seems to mean 'more than only'; it is the definition, meaning unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means fair and equitable, so something not just is unfair or unjust.
